statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail holds at 20%, the floor of the watch band, because the Nasdaq-100 continues to trade on an orderly two-way path: the cash index is 30,520.68, up 0.37% on the day, 246 points above the rejected 30,274.65 session low and 96 points below a 30,616.24 high set within the last hour. VIX has decayed to 16.77 from a 17.59 session high and the 10-year Treasury yield is 5.24% after peaking at 5.34%, its highest since 2002, with the 2-year 44 basis points lower at 4.80%. Stress rises slightly to 75% because the energy and inflation channel worsened within the hour: Brent is $101.99, up 4.04%, and the September ISM prices index jumped 6.8 points to 77.9.
recommendation: Tail remains at 20%, the lower edge of the watch band, and the mapped policy state is unchanged at WATCH. The observed price path is the decisive input: the morning fade has been fully retraced, the index is positive on the day, it has set a marginal new session high at 30,616.24 and then traded back inside the range rather than holding an extreme, and every intraday amplifier that mattered earlier has decayed - VIX from 17.59 to 16.77, the 10-year from 5.34% to 5.24%, the 2-year down 10.8 basis points on the day. Under this contract that combination of genuine retracement and cross-asset stabilisation is grounds for Tail to sit at the band floor, and nothing observed supports a move toward the 25% block threshold. The environment is nonetheless difficult, so Stress rises to 75%: Brent crossed $102 after Chinese refiners suspended October fuel exports, the September ISM prices index jumped to 77.9, 30-year mortgage rates printed 7.28%, and the KBW bank index fell 2.4% intraday even as semiconductors gained 1.4%. The narrow danger window stays on the final US cash hour from 19:00Z to 20:00Z, where late-session continuation or reversal is the next genuine checkpoint; the September payroll report at 12:30Z tomorrow is the following one and is carried in the event calendar rather than in the current action. Scores here are descriptive risk measures only, with no position, sizing or account-specific guidance attached.
headline: Tail holds the 20% watch floor as the Nasdaq-100 retraces a marginal new high; VIX and yields keep decaying while Brent above $102 lifts Stress to 75%
body: The Nasdaq-100 is holding the improvement established earlier in the session. At the 18:35Z cutoff the cash index is 30,520.68 on Yahoo Finance and 30,519.22 on Investing.com, up 0.36-0.37% against a 30,408.50 previous close, so the morning fade is fully retraced and the index is positive on the day. The day's range is 30,274.65 to 30,616.24, a 341-point span: price sits about 246 points above the low it rejected and about 96 points below a high that was marked up from 30,576.44 within the last hour and then given back. That sequence - a marginal new extreme followed by a retracement into the range - is the opposite of the shallow-pullback, repeated-extension structure this contract treats as Tail evidence, and it is why Tail stays at the 20% watch floor rather than advancing. NQ futures are 30,740.00, up 0.13% against the prior settlement and about 210 points above their 30,529.50 session low, so the continuous reference is modestly higher and broadly consistent with cash. Cross-asset amplifiers continue to decay on the equity-relevant axis. VIX is 16.77, still up 2.63% on the day from a 16.34 close but well below the 17.59 session high and only 0.56 above the 16.21 low. The 10-year Treasury yield is 5.24%, down 5.1 basis points on the day after topping 5.34% on Wednesday, its highest level since early 2002, at the end of the worst quarter for the US bond market this century; the 2-year is 4.80%, down 10.8 basis points, and the 30-year is 5.60%. A bull-steepening retreat from a multidecade yield peak reduces, rather than increases, the probability of the delayed-second-leg repricing that would deny mean reversion. Internals are genuinely split, which supports a mixed dominant mode rather than a directional one. Semiconductors lead: SOXX is 576.50, up 1.38%, inside a 564.04 to 579.98 range, with sentiment underpinned by Micron's record fiscal fourth quarter reported on 30 September - revenue of 54.23 billion dollars and non-GAAP EPS of 33.42 dollars, with first-quarter guidance of about 61.5 billion dollars. Against that, the KBW Nasdaq Bank index fell 2.4% intraday, and the broader tape is only fractionally higher with the Dow about flat and the S&P 500 up roughly 0.2%. Conflicting internals of that kind reduce directional conviction; under this contract they raise Stress and temper Confidence rather than mechanically lifting Tail. The difficult part of the environment is the inflation and energy channel, and it worsened within the hour. Brent is 101.99 dollars, up 4.04%, and WTI is 92.63 dollars, up 2.45%, after Chinese refiners suspended October fuel exports for everything except Hong Kong and Macau while Beijing began its week-long national holiday without issuing new permits, tightening a diesel market already disrupted elsewhere. The September ISM manufacturing report released at 14:00Z printed a headline PMI of 54.5 against 54.6 in August, but its prices index jumped 6.8 points to 77.9 and new orders rose to 55.3; 30-year mortgage rates printed 7.28% against 7.03%. Today's labour data was firm: initial jobless claims were 197,000 and the four-week average 200,000. None of that is Tail evidence on its own - event importance, surprise magnitude and generic volatility belong to Stress and Confidence until observed price structure shows mean reversion actually failing - but it does keep Stress at the high end of the band at 75%. Confidence is 88%. Current index, futures, volatility, yield, energy and sector levels were verified directly from primary quote and data sources, today's US releases were confirmed against the issuing report, and the seven-day calendar was verified. The shared Finviz context file was read as required but carried a 29 September collection timestamp and a partial collection status, so it is stale under the 90-minute freshness rule and contributed nothing to this assessment; independent research covered the same ground. The near-term checkpoints are the final US cash hour from 19:00Z to 20:00Z, which is the named danger window, and then the September payroll report at 12:30Z on 2 October with the US cash open following at 13:30Z. Both are carried as conditional risk in the forecast and in the event calendar, not as an assertion that any post-event path has already been observed.

lookbackSummary: Across the preceding 24 hours Claude published an unbroken watch-band regime with a single orange hour. Tail ran between 20% and 25%, reaching the 25% block threshold once in the 06:00Z hour on a trend-up reading before easing back when that structure failed to persist, then touching 24% in the 14:00Z hour as the US cash open reversed the overnight rally. Stress climbed from 70% in the quiet overnight hours to a window high of 78% around the US open and has since eased to 74-76%, tracking the multidecade-high yield backdrop and the energy complex rather than any observed mean-reversion failure. Confidence held in a narrow 87-89% band throughout. The dominant mode was mixed in 22 of the 24 hours, with trend-up only in the 05:00Z and 06:00Z hours. These are the values published at the time and are not restated with hindsight.
outlookSummary: The near path turns on whether the retraced 30,274.65 low and the marginal 30,616.24 high keep bracketing price while volatility and yields continue to decay. Conditional Tail holds 20% for the current hour, ticks to 21% for the 19:00Z final cash hour on late-session continuation or reversal risk, returns to 20% at the 20:00Z close, then decays to 18-19% across the post-close and Asian hours as liquidity thins and the assumed regime becomes quiet consolidation, with Chinese markets shut for the national holiday week. From the 05:00Z European handover the conditional path rebuilds to 20-22% on payroll-day positioning, peaks at 24% - the top of the watch band - across the 12:00Z release hour and the 13:00Z post-release hour that overlaps the US cash open, then eases to 21-23% through the Friday afternoon on the assumption that price discovery becomes orderly once the opening imbalance clears. Conditional Stress peaks at 82-83% around the release because the rates and energy backdrop compounds event risk, while Confidence steps down to 82-84% beyond the European handover because those slots depend on an outcome unknowable at this cutoff. The conditional path never reaches the 25% block threshold: event importance alone does not establish a pathological price path, and Tail would only advance there on observed shallow or failed retracements, repeated extension, or the index holding a session extreme.
